# `silk/concurrency/execution`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Lazy computations with their own storage, which an owner drives and resumes.

## When to use
This module is for schedulers and runtimes. Application code uses `silk.concurrency.fiber` or
`silk.concurrency.thread_pool` instead.

- [`make`](#Execution.impl.make) packages a lazy `Effect` that outlives its caller, for a later owner to run.
- [`drive`](#Execution.impl.drive) runs the first activation, and each later activation after a wake.
- [`park`](#Execution.impl.park) in the body stops it until an external event calls [`wake`](#Execution.impl.wake).

## Details
[`make`](#Execution.impl.make) gets one combined package from the selected `Allocator`. It does not start the
`Effect`. The body, the continuation and the fixed readiness endpoint stay private.

The life of an Execution:

1. `Initial` after [`make`](#Execution.impl.make). `notifyInitial` can mark it ready before the first drive.
2. [`drive`](#Execution.impl.drive) runs the body. It calls `onComplete` with the result, or `onSuspend` with the
   dormant Execution if the body parked.
3. In [`park`](#Execution.impl.park), the body gives its one [`Wake`](#Wake) to a registration callback, and stops.
4. [`wake`](#Execution.impl.wake) makes the Execution eligible and calls the readiness endpoint. The owner then drives
   it again.

A nested `Effect.suspend` transfers execution at once. Only [`park`](#Execution.impl.park) gives up the Execution
until a [`Wake`](#Wake).

The readiness phase and the park generation are in one control word of the package. Each
transition is one compare-exchange of that word. Thus a Wake can come from another thread, and
readiness is published before the endpoint runs (EXEC-009).

For an Execution that moves between threads, use [`makeTransferable`](#Execution.impl.makeTransferable). Its handle is a
[`TransferableExecution`](#TransferableExecution). Its body parks with [`parkTransferable`](#Execution.impl.parkTransferable), and any thread can signal
the [`TransferableWake`](#TransferableWake) (EXEC-010).

## Errors
[`make`](#Execution.impl.make) fails with `OutOfMemoryError` if the package cannot be allocated. Growth of the private
execution stack later is a fatal trap, not an error.

## Gotchas
- `Execution` is affine. The readiness callback must be detached and non-parking.
- Dropping a dormant Execution cancels it.
- A Wake that you keep also keeps the complete inert package alive, until the Wake is used or
  dropped.
- Only `onSuspend` gets the Execution back from [`drive`](#Execution.impl.drive).

## Examples
### Make and drive one Execution
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.concurrency.execution { Execution }

// What the owner sees after one drive.
struct Run {
  done: bool,
  result: i32,
}

// The readiness endpoint. A Wake calls it when a parked body can continue.
fn ready(state: &()) -> () {}

fn completed(state: &mut Run, value: i32) -> () {
  state.done = true
  state.result = value
}

fn suspended(state: &mut Run, execution: Intrinsic.Execution<i32>) -> () {
  // A real owner keeps the dormant Execution, and drives it again after the Wake.
  drop execution
}

effect fn body() -> i32 {
  return 6 * 7
}

effect fn program() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()

  // make allocates the package. The body does not start yet.
  let execution = run Execution.make(body(), (), ready)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let mut state = Run { done: false, result: 0 }

  // drive runs the body. It calls exactly one of the two callbacks.
  run Execution.drive(move execution, &mut state, completed, suspended)
  if !state.done || state.result != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn outOfMemory(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 1
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(program(), outOfMemory)
}
```

<a id="Wake"></a>

## `Wake`

```silk
pub struct Wake
```

The affine readiness authority for one parked generation of one Execution.

### Details

[`Execution.park`](#Execution.impl.park) passes the generation's only Wake to its registration callback.
[`Execution.wake`](#Execution.impl.wake) consumes it and makes that generation eligible at most once.

### Gotchas

Dropping a Wake publishes nothing. A retained Wake keeps the inert package allocation alive
after the Execution is dropped, until the Wake is consumed or dropped.

<a id="TransferableWake"></a>

## `TransferableWake`

```silk
pub struct TransferableWake
```

A Wake that can move to another thread and be signaled there.

### Details
[`Execution.parkTransferable`](#Execution.impl.parkTransferable) passes the only TransferableWake of a generation to its
registration callback. [`Execution.wakeTransferable`](#Execution.impl.wakeTransferable) consumes it on any thread.

### Gotchas
Dropping it publishes nothing. A kept one keeps the inert package allocation alive after the
Execution is dropped, until it is consumed or dropped.

## `TransferableExecution`

```silk
pub struct TransferableExecution<A>
```

The owner of an Execution that [`Execution.makeTransferable`](#Execution.impl.makeTransferable) made. It can move to another
thread.

### Details
[`local`](#TransferableExecution.impl.local) gives back the `Intrinsic.Execution<A>` handle that [`Execution.drive`](#Execution.impl.drive) takes.
[`adopt`](#TransferableExecution.impl.adopt) wraps a handle again, such as the dormant one that `onSuspend` gets. The wrapper is
`Transferable` when `A` is.

### Gotchas
Adopting a handle that [`Execution.make`](#Execution.impl.make) made is a fatal trap.

### Method `notifyInitial`

```silk
pub fn notifyInitial(self: &mut Self) -> ()
```

Notifies the fixed readiness endpoint for one `Initial` Execution exactly once.

#### Details

It changes the package to `InitialReady` before it invokes the endpoint. It is synchronous,
does not park, and does not run the body. A later [`Execution.drive`](#Execution.impl.drive) starts the body.

#### Gotchas

The Execution must still be `Initial`. Calling this operation again, or calling it after the
Execution has been driven, parked, completed, or destroyed, is a fatal state trap.

<a id="Execution"></a>

## `Execution`

```silk
pub struct Execution
```

The owner of the execution lifecycle operations: lazy computations with their own storage,
which an owner drives and resumes.

### When to use

This type is for schedulers and runtimes. Application code uses `silk.concurrency.fiber` or
`silk.concurrency.thread_pool` instead. [`Execution.make`](#Execution.impl.make) packages a lazy `Effect` for a later owner to
run. [`Execution.drive`](#Execution.impl.drive) runs the first activation, and each later activation after a wake.
[`Execution.park`](#Execution.impl.park) in the body stops it until an external event calls [`Execution.wake`](#Execution.impl.wake). For
an Execution that moves between threads, use [`Execution.makeTransferable`](#Execution.impl.makeTransferable).

### Details

The life of an Execution:

1. `Initial` after `make`. `notifyInitial` can mark it ready before the first drive.
2. `drive` runs the body. It calls `onComplete` with the result, or `onSuspend` with the dormant
   Execution if the body parked.
3. In `park`, the body gives its one [`Wake`](#Wake) to a registration callback, and stops.
4. `wake` makes the Execution eligible and calls the readiness endpoint. The owner then drives
   it again.

A nested `Effect.suspend` transfers execution at once. Only `park` gives up the Execution until
a Wake.

This struct carries no data and is never constructed by the library. Every operation is an
inherent member declared in `impl Execution`, so `import silk.concurrency.execution { Execution }` is the
one import that reaches `Execution.make(...)` and the rest. It is unrelated to the builtin
`Intrinsic.Execution<A>` type.

<a id="Execution.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect<'static> fn make<
    A,
    F: once Effect<'static; A> + Intrinsic.Detached,
    O: Intrinsic.Detached,
    R: fn<'static>(&O) -> () + Intrinsic.Detached + Intrinsic.NonParking
  >(body: F, readyState: O, onReady: R) -> Intrinsic.Execution<A>
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Allocates one combined package and transfers the lazy body and fixed endpoint into it.

#### Details

The package comes from the selected `Allocator`. The body, the continuation and the fixed
readiness endpoint stay private.
The returned Execution is `Initial`. The body does not start during this call. Allocation
refusal produces no Execution and leaves every input under ordinary Effect cleanup. Later
private stack growth is a fatal trap and is not a `OutOfMemoryError`.

#### Gotchas

The Execution is affine. The readiness callback must be detached and non-parking. Dropping a
dormant Execution cancels it.

<a id="Execution.impl.makeTransferable"></a>

### Associated function `makeTransferable`

```silk
pub effect<'static> fn makeTransferable<
    A: Transferable,
    F: once Effect<'static; A> + Intrinsic.Detached + Transferable,
    O: Intrinsic.Detached + Transferable + Concurrent,
    R: fn<'static>(&O) -> () + Intrinsic.Detached + Intrinsic.NonParking + Transferable + Concurrent
  >(body: F, readyState: O, onReady: R) -> TransferableExecution<A>
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Allocates one package whose handle and Wakes can move to other threads.

#### Details
The returned Execution is `Initial`, the body does not start during this call, and allocation
refusal produces no Execution. The body and
the result must be `Transferable`, because
the body can resume on any thread that drives it. The endpoint and its state must be
`Transferable` and `Concurrent`, because each [`TransferableWake`](#TransferableWake) runs the endpoint on the
thread that signals it. The body parks with [`parkTransferable`](#Execution.impl.parkTransferable).

#### Gotchas
Values that the body makes itself need no bound. Silk has no thread-local or global storage,
so nothing outside the body can reach them while it moves between threads.

<a id="Execution.impl.drive"></a>

### Associated function `drive`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn drive<
    'env,
    A: 'env,
    D: 'env,
    C: once fn<'env>(D, A) -> () + Intrinsic.NonParking,
    S: once fn<'env>(D, Intrinsic.Execution<A>) -> () + Intrinsic.NonParking
  >(
    execution: Intrinsic.Execution<A>,
    branchState: D,
    onComplete: C,
    onSuspend: S
  ) -> ()
```

Drives one `Initial`, `InitialReady` or `Eligible` activation, and gives `branchState` to one
outcome callback.

#### Details
Completion calls `onComplete`. If the body gives up the Execution, `onSuspend` gets the
dormant Execution. Each activation calls exactly one callback. A nested transfer can complete
in the same drive. An external park gives up ownership until the readiness endpoint reports
that the Execution is eligible.

The body starts its own diagnostic invocation. To keep an observer across parks, install it
inside the body. The outcome callbacks run in the diagnostic context of the caller.

#### Gotchas
Driving a dormant, notifying, completed or destroyed Execution is a fatal state trap. Only
`onSuspend` gets the Execution back.

<a id="Execution.impl.park"></a>

### Associated function `park`

```silk
pub effect fn park<
    'env,
    G,
    F: once fn<'env>(Wake) -> G + Intrinsic.NonParking
  >(register: F) -> ()
```

Relinquishes the currently Running Execution until one external readiness signal arrives.

#### Details

The registration callback receives the generation's sole affine [`Wake`](#Wake). Its returned guard
is retained while dormant and dropped immediately before source continues after this call.
A Wake signaled during registration is latched until [`drive`](#Execution.impl.drive) returns this Execution to its
owner, which then notifies. The Wake invokes the fixed readiness endpoint at most one time.

#### Gotchas

A caller that keeps a cancelled Wake also keeps the complete inert Execution package alive.
Consuming or dropping that Wake releases the final package authority.

<a id="Execution.impl.parkTransferable"></a>

### Associated function `parkTransferable`

```silk
pub effect fn parkTransferable<
    'env,
    G,
    F: once fn<'env>(TransferableWake) -> G + Intrinsic.NonParking
  >(register: F) -> ()
```

Gives up the running Execution and passes a [`TransferableWake`](#TransferableWake) to `register`.

#### Details
Use it in a body that [`makeTransferable`](#Execution.impl.makeTransferable) made. The registration callback receives the
generation's only Wake, which can go to another thread and be signaled there with
[`wakeTransferable`](#Execution.impl.wakeTransferable). A Wake signaled during registration is latched until [`drive`](#Execution.impl.drive) returns
this Execution to its owner. The Wake invokes the fixed readiness endpoint at most one time.

#### Gotchas
A call from a body that [`make`](#Execution.impl.make) made is a fatal state trap, because that endpoint cannot run
on another thread.

<a id="Execution.impl.interrupt"></a>

### Associated function `interrupt`

```silk
pub fn interrupt<A>(execution: &mut Intrinsic.Execution<A>, token: usize) -> ()
```

Asks a parked Execution to resume the interruptible boundary for `token`.

#### Details

A dormant Execution becomes eligible and its readiness endpoint runs, as for a [`wake`](#Execution.impl.wake). An
eligible one keeps its place. When it is next driven, every frame above the boundary that
`Intrinsic.interruptibleEffect` opened for `token` is abandoned from its suspension point,
innermost first, which runs its `Drop` hooks and non-parking finalizers. Then the boundary
resumes with `false`. Wakes of the interrupted park publish nothing.

#### Gotchas

The parked body must be inside a boundary for `token`, and `token` must not be 0. With no
such boundary, every frame is abandoned, as when the Execution is dropped. Interrupting an
Execution that is not dormant or eligible is a fatal state trap.

<a id="Execution.impl.interruptHeld"></a>

### Associated function `interruptHeld`

```silk
pub fn interruptHeld<A>(execution: &mut Intrinsic.Execution<A>, token: usize) -> bool
```

Asks a parked Execution that the caller holds under its own lock to resume the interruptible
boundary for `token`, and returns whether the caller must now queue it.

#### When to use

Use it in an owner whose readiness endpoint takes the same lock, so [`interrupt`](#Execution.impl.interrupt) would
deadlock, and which stores each parked Execution before [`drive`](#Execution.impl.drive) returns, so the park may
still be registering.

#### Details

It stores the token as [`interrupt`](#Execution.impl.interrupt) does, with three differences. A dormant Execution becomes
eligible without running its readiness endpoint, and the call returns `true`, so the caller
queues it. A park that is still registering, as in the `onSuspend` callback of [`drive`](#Execution.impl.drive), is
latched, so `drive` notifies the endpoint once it returns. An Execution that already holds a smaller token keeps it: with tokens that grow
with each boundary, that is the outer one.

#### Gotchas

`token` must not be 0. The boundary rules of [`interrupt`](#Execution.impl.interrupt) apply. Interrupting an Execution
that is not parked is a fatal state trap.

<a id="Execution.impl.wakeTransferable"></a>

### Associated function `wakeTransferable`

```silk
pub fn wakeTransferable(wake: TransferableWake) -> ()
```

Consumes one TransferableWake on any thread, and makes its parked generation eligible.

#### Details
A Wake signaled while its generation is still registering is latched until the owner receives
the Execution back from [`drive`](#Execution.impl.drive). A Wake signaled while its generation is dormant makes the
Execution eligible and invokes its fixed readiness endpoint on the calling thread. Signaling
never drives the Execution. A Wake for a dropped or completed Execution, or for an earlier
generation, publishes nothing.

<a id="Execution.impl.wake"></a>

### Associated function `wake`

```silk
pub fn wake(wake: Wake) -> ()
```

Consumes one Wake and makes its parked generation eligible.

#### Details

A Wake signaled while its generation is still registering is latched until the owner receives
the Execution back from [`drive`](#Execution.impl.drive). A Wake signaled while its generation is dormant makes the
Execution eligible and synchronously invokes its fixed readiness endpoint. Signaling never
drives the Execution.

#### Gotchas

A Wake for a dropped or completed Execution, or for an earlier generation, publishes nothing
and only releases its package authority.
